prompt: A builder cuts two triangular roof trusses. All three sides of the first truss are exactly as long as the three matching sides of the second. Which congruence criterion proves the trusses are congruent? Answer with three letters.
hint: List what is known to match in the two trusses. How many pairs of sides are there, and how many pairs of angles?

hints.text: List what is known to match in the two trusses. How many pairs of sides are there, and how many pairs of angles?
Three pairs of sides match and no angles are used, so the name has one letter S for each pair of sides.
Three pairs of equal sides is the SSS criterion, short for Side-Side-Side.

explanation: All three pairs of corresponding sides are congruent, and no angle measurements are needed at all.
Three matching sides is exactly the Side-Side-Side criterion, so the trusses are congruent by SSS.
This works because three fixed side lengths can only form one triangle shape, which is why builders trust triangular trusses.

alternativeExplanations.title: Try to build a different one
steps: Cut three sticks of set lengths and join them end to end into a triangle.
No matter how you wiggle them, you always get the same shape — you can flip it or turn it, but you cannot change it. That rigidity is SSS.
